Τhe audit time provided in the audit time chart shall not be reduced by more than 30%. Τhe time calculated for planning and report writing combined should not typically reduce the total on-site “audit time” to less than 70% of the time calculated (in accordance with B.3.3 and B.3.4. of ISO/IEC 27006:2015). Certification bodies may consider using a sample-based approach to multiple-site certification audit: a. all sites are operating under the same ISMS, which is centrally administered and audited and subject to central management review b. all sites are included within the client’s internal ISMS audit programme c. all sites are included within the client’s ISMS management review programme In case of multi-site organizations, a representative number of sites have been sampled taking into account: the results of internal audits of head office and the sites the results of management review variations in the size of the sites variations in the business purpose of the sites complexity of the ISMS complexity of the information systems at the different sites variations in working practices variations in activities undertaken potential interaction with critical information systems or information systems processing sensitive information any differing legal requirements The number of total on-site auditor days – as calculated in the above Audit Time Chart – shall be distributed amongst the different sites based on the relevance of the site for the management system and the risks identified. The total time expended on initial audit and surveillance is the total sum of the time spent at each site plus the central office and shall never be less than that which would have been calculated for the size and complexity of the operation if all the work had been undertaken at a single site (i.e., with all the employees of the company in the same site).

Effective number of personnel is calculated as described in MS Audit mandays calculation procedure (VB-BA-ZET-MS-All-003-MDC-EN). In case of seasonal operations (e.g. harvesting activities, holiday villages and hotels, etc,) the calculation of the effective number of personnel shall be based on the personnel typically present in peak season operations. Especially for OH&SMS the following factors shall be considered in order to determine effective personnel number: it shall also include personnel from contractors and subcontractors performing work or work-related activities that are under the control or influence of the organization, that can have impact on the organization’s OH&SMS performance. in case of seasonal operations (e.g. harvesting activities, holiday villages and hotels, etc.) the calculation of the effective number of personnel shall be based on the personnel typically present in peak season operations. reductions due to employment of large numbers of unskilled personnel shall be regarded as not applicable, since the employment of temporary unskilled personnel can be a source of OH&S risks. If, in exceptional cases, a reduction is made, the justification for doing so shall be recorded. When a high percentage of personnel (≥20% per activity position) perform certain activities/positions that are considered similar or identical, because they expose personnel to similar OH&S risks (e.g. cleaners, security, sales, call centers, etc.), a reduction in the number of personnel which is coherent and consistently applied on a company to company basis within the scope of certification is permitted, according to the following reductions apply to the number of the relevant per activity/position personnel: For personnel working on shifts, timing of the audit shall be determined in a way that will best assess the effective implementation of the OH&SMS for the full scope of the client activities, including the need to audit outside normal working hours and various shift patterns. This shall be agreed with the client. To audit effective implementation, at least one of the shifts inside and one outside of regular office hours shall be audited during the first cycle of certification. Adjustments for delaying the starting time of audit can be made in order to cover both shifts within the 8 hours audit time. However, it must be ensured that any variation in audit time does not compromise the effectiveness of audits. At least one of the shifts inside and one outside of regular office hours shall be audited during the first cycle of certification if the client organization operates in more than one shift. Auditing outside normal working hours and various shift patterns will be agreed in advance with the client. During surveillance audits of the subsequent cycles, it is possible not to audit the second shift based on the recognized maturity of the OH&SMS. The justification for not auditing the other shifts shall be documented to the audit plan taking into account the risk for not doing so. Criteria for auditing other shifts are the following: Higher rate of injuries Larger number of unskilled personnel Presence of more dangerous materials than those on other shifts Higher complexity of processes Adjustments for delaying the starting time of audit are recommended whenever possible, in order to cover both shifts within the audit day. The justification for not auditing the other shifts shall be documented taking into account the risk for not doing so.

Sampling of sites is permitted only for organizations fulfilling the conditions described in VB-BA-ZET-MS-All-003-Ann-MSOSG-EN - Multisite Organisation Sampling Guidance. Further to the guidance requirements, for OHSMS the following apply: Sampling of sites is permitted only if sites are covering the same activities, processes and OH&S risks. Where sampling is appropriate, differences between the operations of each site will be taken into account in order to decide the sites to be audited. The sample of sites (including temporary sites) should represent the client’s scope of certification, sizes and types of activities and processes, type of hazards involved and associated OH&S risks, and stages of projects in progress. The decision if site sampling is permitted or not, shall be based on the evaluation of the level of OH&S risks associated with the activities and processes carried out in each site included in the scope of certification. Records of such evaluations and rationale of decisions taken shall be kept. Sampling of sites that are not covering the same activities, processes and OH&S risks is not allowed. In addition, processes control and OH&S risk control cannot be audited using remote or similar audit techniques, but only on-site.

Complexity categories for an OHSMS audit are based on the nature, number and severity of risks for occupational health and safety. These categories affect the audit duration (see Table 2) and are shown below: High: sites with complex technology / processes with high risk that require special protection measures / processes with heavy machinery (e.g excavators) / processes that can only be carried out by specialized personnel / large quantity of hazardous material (special conditions of storage) / significant risks relevant to the products / processes that involve high risk of fire. Medium: medium number of processes that require special protection measures / limited number of processes that require special training for risks relevant to the products / processes that involve risk of fire Low: processes with low risk where special protection measures are not required / small quantities of hazardous material (no requirement for specific storage facilities) The complexity category of OH&S risk of an organization may also be associated to the consequences of a failure in the capability of the OH&SMS to control the risk: High – where failure to manage the risk could put life at risk or result in serious injury. Medium – where failure to manage the risk could result in injury or illness. Low – where failure to manage the risk is may result in minor injury or illness. Risk categories for a QMS audit are based on the nature of activities of the organization. These categories affect the audit duration and are shown below. It is expected that business activities defined as low risk may require less audit time than the time calculated using Table 1, activities defined as medium risk will take the time calculated using Table 1, and activities defined as high risk will take more time. The reduction of audit time of management systems shall not exceed 30% of the times established from Table 1. These risk categories are not definitive, they are examples only that could be used when determining the risk category of an audit High risk : Where failure of the product or service causes economic catastrophe or puts life at risk. Medium risk : Where failure of the product or service could cause injury or illness. Low risk : Where failure of the product or service is unlikely to cause injury or illness. For organizations with activities that fall into more than one risk categories, the calculation of mandays is the sum of the required mandays for each activity based on the number of employees in each category. Activities considered to be of high risk
Client is not "design responsible" or other standard elements are not covered in the scope
Very small site for number of personnel (e.g. office complex only),
Prior knowledge of the client management system (e.g., already certified to another standard by the same CAB);
Client preparedness for certification (e.g., already certified or recognized by another 3rd party scheme);

Where staff include a number of people who work “off location” e.g. salespersons, drivers, service personnel, etc. and it is possible to substantially audit compliance of their activities with the system through review of records
Activities considered to be of low risk
Processes involving similar and repetitive activities
Identical activities of low complexity performed on all shifts with appropriate evidence of equivalent performance on all shifts
Where significant proportion of the staff carry out a similar simple function. Repetitive processes within the scope.

ISO2000;2018 total audit duration for a single site: Ds = (TD + TH + TFTE) calculated according to ISO 22003-1:2022 Where: -TD is the basic on-site audit time -TH is the audit days for additional HACCP studies -TFTE is the audit days per number of FTE employees Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day for ISO22000:2018 FSSC2000 v6 total audit duration for a single site: Ds + TFSSC + any other additional Where: -Ds = (TD + TH + TFTE) calculated according to ISO 22003-1:2022 (see above) -TFSSC shall be calculated as follows: 1 auditor day (8 working hours) when the company has less than 250 FTE and 1 or 2 HACCP studies 1,5 auditor day (12 working hours) when the company has 250 FTE or more; or 3 HACCP studies or more -Any other additional (see below: about Head Office and off-site activities) Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day for FSSC22000 v6 Minimum audit duration for FSSC22000 v6 is 2 days for all food chain categories. For FII a minimum audit duration of 1,5 day may be applied. Exemption to the minimum audit duration applied to organizations with simple processes, less than 20FTE and 1HACCP study, the minimum audit duration is allowed to be 1,5 day for all audit types. If after the calculation the result is a decimal number, the exact hours may be used or where rounding is applied to the number of days, this shall be rounded upwards to the nearest half day (e.g. 5.3 audit days becomes 5.5 audit day).

The duration of an audit day normally is 8 hours and may be longer than 8 hours but shall never exceed 10 hours and only in accordance with the relevant International Labor Organisation and national legislative requirements. The audit duration shall only apply to qualified auditors and not to other team members (eg. Witnessors, trainees, technical experts, observers, interpreters). A HACCP study corresponds to a hazard analysis for a family of products/services with similar hazards and similar production technology and, where relevant, similar storage technology. Audit duration does not include time for audit planning, audit preparation, travel to and from site, audit follow-up activities if there are nonconformities, or team member(s) not assigned as an auditor (i.e. technical experts, translators, interpreters, observers and auditors-in-training, and report writers). A minimum 50 % of total audit duration shall be spent on auditing the operational food safety planning and the implementation of PRPs and control measures. Operational food safety planning does not include activities related to FSMS development, training, internal audit, management review and improvement. If there are multiple categories or subcategories, use the category or subcategory with the highest TD value to determine Ds. The combined parameters (HACCP study, FTE) for all the categories/subcategories shall be used when calculating the audit duration When determining the number of employees involved in any aspect of food safety, it shall be expressed as the number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees. When an organization deploys workers in shifts and the products and/or processes are similar, the FTE number will be calculated based on employees on the main shift (including seasonal workers) plus non-production staff having an impact on food safety. Reduction for ISO22000:2018 audits: In cases of a FSMS which is integrated or in combination with another relevant management system (eg.ISO9001, ISO14001) or food safety system (FSS), a reduction in audit duration is possible. The combined audit duration shall be determined and recorded as follows: — calculate the audit duration for each scheme separately (including scheme restrictions and allowed reductions); — add the audit durations together; — determine the degree of reduction considering a maximum of 20 % reduction can be made on the combined duration. The reduction range based on integration is 0 % to 20 % determined by the level of integration of overall business strategy, management reviews, approach to policy, objectives, systems, processes, internal audits and effective corrective action to prevent reoccurrence. Reduction for FSSC22000 v6 audits: When properly documented and justified, a reduction of the Ds audit duration can be made in accordance with ISO22003-1;2022 annex B. The reduced Ds audit duration can never be more than 0,25 auditor day (2 working hours) and the Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day. The reduction cannot be applied on the TFSSC. Justification of the audit duration calculation including any applied reduction or increase shall be included in the audit report. Preparation and reporting time is not included in ISO22000;2018 nor FSSC2200 v6 audit duration. Specially for FSSC2200 v6 preparation and reporting time shall be in addition to the audit duration. Where more than one food chain category is included in the scope of the certification, additional reporting time may be required, based on the audit complexity. Specially for FSSC2200 v6, the below refers to the minimum time to be allocated: At least 0.25 auditor day (2 working hours) for audit preparation. At least 1 auditor day (8 working hours) for audit reporting Use of an interpreter: Additional time shall be considered in case an interpreter (assigned by the CB and be independent of the organisation audited) is required to support the audit team. Where an interpreter is required to support the audit team, the audit duration of the relevant audit or audit part (in cases where the interpreter is not present for the full audit duration), shall be increased with at least 20% to allow for the translation process. In determining the audit duration, among other things, the following aspects may increase the audit duration: the complexity of the client activities (e.g number of product types and process types, production line number, number of people or type, variety of tasks affecting food safety, product development, sanitation, laboratory analysis within the audited company), and its FSMS, the hazards associated, statutory and regulatory context, any outsourcing included in the scope of certification, the maturity and effectiveness of the FSMS, the results of the prior audits, the size/infrastructure, geographical location. In determining the audit duration, among other things, the following aspects are considered: the seasonality, the multi-site and centralised control of the FSMS, the level of automation, closed production systems, use of technology, mechanisation and labour intensiveness, whether audit is combined, joint, integrated or stand alone, audit delivery method (eg. For ICT see relevant procedure) Where the ICT Audit Approach is utilized for FSSC remote audits, the especial requirements of VB-BA-ZET-MS-All-004-AUSE-FSSC Procedure applies

Stages 1 and 2 are included in the minimum initial certification audit time. In exceptional circumstances or events, all or part of stage 1 can take place off-site or remotely through the use of ICT and shall be fully justified. The evidence demonstrating that stage 1 objectives are fully achieved shall be provided. NOTE: Exceptional circumstances or events can include a very remote location, a natural disaster, a pandemic, a short seasonal production and other special situations. NOTE: Any part of the FSMS that is audited during the stage 1 audit, and determined to be fully implemented, effective and in conformity with requirements, does not necessarily need to be re-audited during stage 2. In this case, the audit report includes these findings and clearly states that conformity has been established during the stage 1 of the audit. The interval between stage 1 and stage 2 shall not be longer than six months. Stage 1 shall be repeated if a longer interval is needed Any part of the FSMS that is audited during stage 1, and determined to be fully implemented, effective and in conformity with requirements, does not necessarily need to be re-audited during stage 2. In this case, the audit report includes these findings and clearly states that conformity has been established during the stage 1 audit. The audit will be conducted over a continuous number of days, excluding weekends when it is not a working day and public holidays It is the organisation’s responsibility to communicate any local holidys or shut downs in a timely manner to facilitate audit scheduling The audit shall be carried out in a mutually agreed language. If an interpreter may be needed extra audit time occurs

ISO 22000:2018 Surveillance audit duration = 1/3 x Ds Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day and 0,5 audit day for categories A and B FSSC22000 v6 Surveillance audit duration = (1/3 x Ds) + TFSSC + any other additional (see below) Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day for FSSC22000 v6 Minimum audit duration for FSSC22000 v6 is 2 days for all food chain categories. For FII a minimum audit duration of 1,5 day may be applied. Exemption to the minimum audit duration applied to organizations with simple processes, less than 20FTE and 1HACCP study, the minimum audit duration is allowed to be 1,5 day for all audit types. If after the calculation the result is a decimal number, the exact hours may be used or where rounding is applied to the number of days, this shall be rounded upwards to the nearest half day (e.g. 5.3 audit days becomes 5.5 audit day).
Surveillance General Requirements only for FSSC22000

Each surveillance audit is a full system audit and covers all the scheme requirements The date of the first surveillance audit, after the initial certification, shall not exceed 12 months from the initial certification decision date, otherwise the certification shall be suspended. One surveillance (eg. the 2nd surveillance) audit is undertaken unannounced after the initial certification audit and within 3 year period thereafter An unannounced FSSC22000 audit is required per 3 year period, either there are any other GFSI unannounced audits conducted at the same 3 year period or not The initial certification audit cannot be unannounced In cases where specific visa or security restrictions apply, then a time window of 30 days shall be notified to the company Blackout days may be agreed in advance with the company All scheme requirements shall be assessed including production or service processes in operation. Where parts of the audit plan cannot be audited, an announced follow up audit shall be scheduled within 28 calendar days, whilst still meeting the calendar year requirement If the organization refuses to participate in the unannounced audit, the certificate shall be suspended within 3 working days of the date of refusal. The certificate shall be withdrawn if the unannounced audit is not conducted within a six-month period from the date of suspension. The audit of separate Head Offices controlling certain FSMS processes pertinent to certification separate to the site, this should be announced. If Head Office activities are part of the site audit, is shall be unannounced. Off-site activities, off-site storage, warehouses and distribution facilities shall also be audited during the unannounced audit. During an unannounced audit the production facilities and premises should be audited within 1 hour after the auditor has arrived on site. In case of multiple buildings at the site the auditor shall, based on risk, decide which buildings/facilities shall be inspected in which order. The unannounced audit takes please during normal operational working hours with consideration of all shifts, where applicable. Where a certified organization moves to another location, at least a stage2 audit shall be conducted, resulting in the start of a new 3-year certification cycle. The audit will be conducted over a continuous number of days, excluding weekends when it is not a working day and public holidays It is the organisation’s responsibility to communicate any local holidays or shut downs in a timely manner to facilitate audit scheduling The audit shall be carried out in a mutually agreed language. If an interpreter may be needed extra audit time occurs.

ISO 22000:2018 Recertification audit duration = 2/3 x Ds Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day and 0,5 audit day for categories A and B FSSC22000 v6 Recertification audit duration = (2/3 x Ds) + TFSSC + any other additional (see below) Ds cannot be reduced below 1 day for FSSC22000 v6 Minimum audit duration for FSSC22000 v6 is 2 days for all food chain categories. For FII a minimum audit duration of 1,5 day may be applied. Exemption to the minimum audit duration applied to organizations with simple processes, less than 20FTE and 1HACCP study, the minimum audit duration is allowed to be 1,5 day for all audit types. If after the calculation the result is a decimal number, the exact hours may be used or where rounding is applied to the number of days, this shall be rounded upwards to the nearest half day (e.g. 5.3 audit days becomes 5.5 audit day).
Recertification General Requirements only for FSSC22000

Recertification audits shall take place preferably at least 3 months prior to the expiry date of the certificate Where the certificate expires prior to the recertification activities being undertaken, the CB can restore certification within 6 months, provided that the outstanding recertification activities are completed, otherwise a full initial audit (stage1 and stage 2) shall be conducted. Recertification audits are full system audits against the Scheme requirements The audit will be conducted over a continuous number of days, excluding weekends when it is not a working day and public holidays It is the organisation’s responsibility to communicate any local holidays or shut downs in a timely manner to facilitate audit scheduling The audit shall be carried out in a mutually agreed language. If an interpreter may be needed extra audit time occurs
Additional Audit time only for FSSC22000

Additional time shall be required for the following situations: a) Head Office (eg. procurement, product development, supplier approval, quality assurance etc but still part of the same legal entity or part of the same larger organisation) i. For organizations where some functions pertinent to the certification are controlled by a Head Office separate to the site (and when these functions are audited prior to the site audit), the minimum time shall be 0.5 auditor day (4 working hours) to audit the functions pertinent to the certification at the Head Office. Increased audit duration may apply depending on the nature, complexity, sites linked to the Head Office etc. No additional audit time is needed when Head Office functions are assessed as part of the site. ii. Where it is not possible to audit these functions and access information during the site audit, a separate head office audit shall be conducted prior to the site audit. The subsequent audit at the site shall include confirmation that the requirements are met and if certain topics should be followed up all information from the Head Office should be available iii. The site audit report shall include which FSMS functions and/or processes have been audited at the Head Office, including the information and supporting objective evidences. iv. When the same Head Office is linked to more than one site, the Head Office audit is conducted before other audits within a 12 month period, but as close to the site audits as possible and a separate audit report should be uploaded in the Assurance portal together with each site audit report. A 20% reduction can be allowed for each of the single sites Ds. v. Every site linked to the Head Office shall have a separate audit, audit report and certificate. vi. The Head Office shall be audited at every audit type (initial, surveillance, recertification). The audit may be conducted onsite or remotely based on the feasibility assessment and in accordance with FSSC22000 v6 Annex 5 vii. NCs identified at the Head Office shall be part of the Audit Report viii. The Head Office cannot receive a separate certificate as the functions/processes audited are part of the site’s audit. The Head Office is referenced on the site certificate, regardless of whether assessed as part of the site audit or as a separate audit, and shall indicate which FSMS functions and/or process have been managed. b) Off-site activities i. For organizations where some functions (manufacturing, processing or service process, all part of the same legal entity and under the same FSMS) is spit across more than one physical address, these locations may be covered in one audit. This is limited to 2 sites (main and satellite site) or to a campus style set up, all in the same country and the audit must be delivered in a continuous manner that is in accordance with the audit duration calculated. ii. Storage facilities (part of the same legal entity and under the same FSMS) at another location shall also be included in the same audit provided that only storage of the site’s products are stored. Where activities or services are provided for other customers separate certification will be required. iii. The certificate shall include the audited locations with activities per location and audit report shall clearly reflect what is audited at each location including a sufficient level of objective evidences. iv. Where off site manufacturing, processing or service activities take place, a 50% audit time reduction of Ds may be applied for each satellite site OR the parameters (eg. FTE, HACCP studies) of the satellite site shall be included in the main site audit duration calculation and travel time between locations shall be included in the audit plan. v. Where off site storage take place, at least 0,25 auditor day (2 working hours) additional audit time shall be added to the FSSC 22000 audit duration for each off-site storage facility or cross docking. vi. Transshipment is not covered in this requirement.
Transition from ISO22000:2018 to FSSC2200 v6

When transitioning an ISO 22000 or a GFSI recognized certification (valid at the time of the transition audit with an equivalent scope) to FSSC certification, the minimum audit duration of the transition audit shall be 2/3 of the Ds + the TFSSC + all additional audit times. Stage 1 may be performed at the discretion of the CB The valid ISO22000 or equivalent GFSI recognised certificate does not have to be issued by the CB undertaking the transition audit. A successful transition audit shall result in an FSSC22000 certificate with a validity of 3 years.

An auditor is not allowed to perform more than two 3-year certification cycles at the same certified organisation either as a lead or co- auditor. If an auditor starts auditing within a certification cycle, she/he will be rotated out after 6 years, for a minimum of 1 year (excluding stage 1, follow-up or special audits).

A multi-site organisation is an organisation having an identified central function at which certain FSMS activities are planned, controlled or managed, and a network of sites at which such activities are fully or partially carried out, as per ISO220003-1;2022, clause 9.1.5.2 Multi-site certification is only allowed for E, FI, FII, G for FSSC22000 v6 A group certificate is issued, it is not allowed to issue certificates to individual sites For organizations with 20 sites or less, all sites shall be audited. If any site has a major nonconformity and satisfactory corrective action have not been implemented in the agreed time frame, certification shall not be granted or maintained for the whole multi-site organization pending satisfactory corrective action. The certification body shall identify and include in the scope of certification the processes of the FSMS implemented at each sampled site. Where sites are added to the group, an audit is required before adding them to the certificate, either as a special audit (scope extension) or as part of the regular audit. During stage 1 audit the central function shall be audited as a minimum, it is recommended to include some of the sites in stage 1 audit. If a site is not audited during stage 1, then the full initial audit duration shall be applied at the stage 2 audit It is recommended that the central function is audited before the sites. In exceptional cases, a small number of the sites may be audited prior to the audit of the central function. The site audits shall be conducted as close to the central function as possible, but always within 12 months of the central function audit. It is recommended to produce one audit report for the multi-site organization, separate reports (for the central function and each site) may also be produced. Once every 3 years, the annual audit will be conducted fully unannounced as this determined in the audit program, including the central function and the sampled site audits It might be necessary to follow up on certain topics with the central function during or after a site audit, in which case the responsible individual/s at the central function shall make the information available.

For organizations with more than 20 sites (initial certification, surveillance and recertification audits): For ISO22000;2018: The use of multi-site sampling is permitted for categories A and B. Sampling may be applied to multi-site organizations, with the minimum sample size being the square root of the total number of sites: √(x), rounded up to the next whole number. The square root sample shall be taken per risk category based on production complexity of the sites (e.g. open field plant production, perennial plant production, indoor production, open field livestock production, indoor livestock production). For ISO22000;2018 & FSSC22000 v6: The use of multi-site sampling is permitted for categories F and G, and only for re-heating-type facilities (e.g. event catering, coffee shops, pubs) for category E and only for facilities with limited preparation or cooking (e.g. re-heating, frying). For organizations with more than 20 sites, the minimum number of sites to be sampled shall be 20 plus the square root of the total number of other sites: y = 20 + √(x – 20), rounded up to the next whole number. This applies to the initial certification, to surveillance and to recertification audits. Where multi-site sampling is permitted, the certification body shall ensure (e.g. via contractual arrangements) that the organization has conducted an internal audit for each site within one year prior to certification and when applicable the effectiveness of corrective actions shall be available. Following certification, the annual internal audit shall cover all sites of the organization included in the certification scope of the multi-site organization and ongoing effectiveness of corrective actions shall be demonstrated The sample shall be partly selective and partly random and shall result in a representative range of different sites being selected, ensuring all processes covered by the scope of certification will be audited. At least 25 % of the sample shall be selected at random. The remainder shall be selected so that the differences among the sites selected over the period of validity of the certification are as large as possible. The certification body shall increase the size of sample or terminate the site sampling where the FSMS subject to certification does not indicate the ability to achieve the intended results. At least annually, an audit of the central office for the FSMS and on the required number of sampled sites shall be performed by the certification body prior to the sampled site audits. At least annually, surveillance audits shall be performed by the certification body on the required number of sampled sites. Audit findings of the sampled sites shall be considered indicative of the entire system and correction shall be implemented accordingly In addition, the risk categories and performance of the sites shall be considered and might result in an increase in the sample size.

For number of HACCP studies use the number of different HACCP studies within the multisite organisation For ISO22000:2018: The site audit duration of the central function shall be equal to or greater than Ds, minimum 1 audit day The site audit duration for each site audited shall be equal to or greater than half of Ds for that site, minimum 1 audit day For FSSC22000 v6: The site audit duration of the central function shall be equal to or greater than Ds, minimum 1 audit day Tfssc is not required to be added to the central function audit duration The site audit duration for each site audited shall be equal to or greater than half of Ds for that site (the reduction is only applied to Ds) The audit duration of each site cannot be below 1.5 auditor day for all audit types (initial, surveillance and recertification) and all applicable food chain categories.

Where the FSSC 22000 audit is undertaken in combination or integration with other food safety audits as a combined audit, the audit time stated in the report shall be of the total combined audit and match the audit plan. Total audit duration is then longer than for FSSC 22000 alone. This is considered as an increase in audit duration and the reason for this shall be justified. The audit duration for the integrated FSSC 22000 and ISO 9001 audit shall be based on Qin_MSPD_003 – Integrated Audit duration, to which TFSSC shall be added.
